newsitem.title: USA: Bishops renew pope's Fla. death row inmate appeal.
newsitem.headline: Bishops renew pope's Fla. death row inmate appeal.

text.p: Florida's Catholic bishops on Thursday joined Pope John Paul II in urging Florida's governor to call off the planned execution next week of a death row inmate convicted of murdering a teacher.

In a letter to Gov. Lawton Chiles, a papal representative appealed for clemency for Pedro Medina, who was scheduled to die in Florida's electric chair on Jan. 29 for the 1982 murder of Dorothy James, an Orlando physical education teacher.

"We express deep sympathy for the victims of murder, for their brutalization and loss of life," the bishops said in a statement reiterating the pope's appeal to Chiles for clemency. "We affirm that the state has the duty to punish criminals ... but we believe that the prevention of crime lies elsewhere than in the death penalty."
The governor's office could not immediately be reached for comment.
In a Jan. 17 letter to Chiles, Archbishop Agostino Cacciavillan, apostolic pro-nuncio for the pope, urged clemency for Medina, who has now exhausted all appeals.

"Committed to upholding the sacredness and dignity of each human life, the Holy Father prays that the life of Mr. Medina may be saved through the compassion and magnanimity of yourself and the board of pardons and paroles," he wrote.
"A gesture of mercy in this case would greatly contribute to the promotion of non-violence and of mutual respect and love in society."
Medina, 39, was slated to die on Dec. 5 but was spared when his attorneys argued that he was insane and did not know the consequences of his actions. The appeal triggered an automatic delay.
After a panel of psychiatrists reviewed the case and found Medina sane, Chiles again issued a death warrant.
Medina was sentenced to death in 1983. The sentence was affirmed by the Florida Supreme Court in 1986 but his appeals in state and federal courts were not finished until last June.
